messages:
mira: Heads up — seeing increased NCCL hangs in us-west-2 on our GPU fleet. Lots of jobs failing with IBV_WQ_FULL / MR reg timeouts. :eyes: Alerting SRE.

srebot: ALERT: nccl_hang_rate > 50/min across us-west-2-gpu-cluster (svc: inference-prod) <https://monitoring.internal/alerts/1122|details>

ash: Which AZ is this spiking in? az-a or az-b? Any pattern with instance type?

mira: Mostly az-b (us-west-2b). Errors show `ibv_exp_send_wr` failures and long MR registration TTR (~2s) before timeout. Affected jobs are multi-GPU NCCL allreduce.

jonas: Can you paste `dmesg` + `ibv_devinfo` from one of the affected hosts? I want to check firmware + port state and GPUDirect errors.

mira: Pasted node logs (truncated):
```
[2026-03-15T10:24:01Z] mlx5_core: mlx5 QoS cfg changed
mlx5 0000:81:00.0: mlx5_core driver: RoCE v2 heartbeat missed on port 1
ib_uhca: failing MR registration: -110
kernel: PFIFO: drop on dev eth0
```

kevin: I also saw asymmetric route counts in our network graphs for az-b during that window. traceroute from worker -> peer shows it leaves via tor1 but return path via tor2 for certain flows.

jonas: That would absolutely break RoCE. RoCE requires symmetric forwarding for PFC/QoS to work end-to-end. If forward/return take different ToRs you can lose heartbeats. Can we check ECMP hashing and BGP next-hops?

ash: Confirmed: there was a BGP flap at 10:17 UTC that changed next-hop for a subset of /24s. ECMP kept flows on old path intermittently, so packets got misrouted. I can push a route-policy to prefer a single next-hop for those prefixes while we stabilize.

mira: What are stopgap options? Disable ECMP for the affected prefixes? Or pin hash to src/dst ports? Customers are seeing degraded training.

ash: Short-term: apply route-policy to force single best-path for ROCE prefixes in az-b. Medium-term: adjust ECMP hash to include src port for better flow affinity and avoid path churn for RDMA-sensitive flows. Rolling change in 5m to `bgp-router-az-b`.

deploy-bot: Runbook action: applied route-policy `fix-roce-az-b` to bgp-router-az-b (change id 512).

jonas: After route-policy, one canary host shows immediate reduction in `ibv` errors and NCCL resumes normal handshakes. Good signal. However MR registration latency still spikes on ~5% of hosts.

kevin: Dug further — 3 of 60 hosts in the pool have older NIC firmware (1.0.9) that is known to mis-handle priority-flow-control under microburst. Scheduling a rolling firmware bump to 1.2.6 (non-disruptive path, requires controlled reboot).

mira: Plan for remediation: 1) keep route-policy in place until BGP is stable; 2) schedule targeted firmware roll for the 3 hosts in the next 24h during low traffic; 3) add an alert for `roce_heartbeat_missed` at 15s resolution; 4) add a per-AZ ECMP-heatmap to console. Thanks everyone.

ash: :thumbsup: will monitor BGP metrics and post updates to incident doc (links in #incidents).

jonas: Adding a small probe job to our canary suite that runs NCCL allreduce every 2m to catch regressions earlier.

mira: Noting: follow-up to add `ibv` metrics to our per-route dashboards and a short postmortem once firmware roll completes.
